stage1.impression: A clean, competent CG render of a small screening room: two glowing red acrylic speakers on oak plinths, rows of identical oak chairs, a dark fluted back wall and a flat salmon floor. The whole frame has a pink-orange cast, the brightest large surfaces are the floor and the left plaster wall rather than the speakers, the felt reads as rigid fluted panelling, and there is no practical lamp, no prop and no sign of life, so it reads as a showroom render. A design magazine would not run it as a specific place: it is a generic listening or screening room.

blocking_9: Neutral surfaces read neutral: the plaster, rug and felt carry no pink or red cast, so the only saturated colour is the Ember pair
The speakers are the brightest objects that matter: speaker region lum_median >= 45 while the rug and the left plaster sit below them
A visible, motivated practical in the frame (a lit Core on the decks table or a Hemisphere) so the light reads as the room's own
The felt reads as heavy, soft, irregularly folded wool felt with nap, not regular vertical fluting with specular lines
The rug and oak show real material at 1:1: wool pile and a bound edge on the rug, a different grain on every chair, natural oak not red stain
Signs of life and a place: the decks table, records, a sleeve, a coat or a glass in frame
A believable lens: 24 to 35 mm at seated eye height, without the stretched left-edge chairs and the cropped chair back filling the bottom right

defects.what: Overall pink-orange cast (median RGB 53/30/19): neutrals do not read neutral, so the Ember pair is not the only colour
The rug is a flat, featureless salmon field (median lum 118, RGB 158/109/83), brighter than the speakers, with no pile, edge or texture at 1:1
The left plaster wall is flat-lit at median 113, the second-brightest surface, and it pulls the eye off the speakers
The felt reads as rigid vertical fluting with thin specular lines and evenly spaced folds; the wash is brightest at the top (78 at the top falling to 18 at speaker height)
Right speaker: region median only 26.7; the cabinet interior is dark and only the red panels glow, so it reads as lit red plastic
Left speaker: median 27, and 1.7% of its pixels are clipped on the red panels
The chairs are identical copies with the same grain placement and a saturated red-brown stain (RGB 124/62/39); the seat pads match the rug, and contact shadows are weak
A cropped chair back fills the bottom right foreground with a blurred brown slab
Wide-lens stretching on the left-edge chairs (20 mm)
Plinth tops are hot (median 100) and lit more than the speakers they carry
No practical lamps, decks table, records or props in frame; nothing says what room this is or that anyone uses it

changes.problem: The frame carries a strong pink-orange cast, so the plaster, rug and felt compete with the Ember speakers for colour.

evidence.measured: plaster RGB median 139/109/83; frame median 53/30/19; rug 158/109/83

change.to: 2700 K, tint +1.0 (toward green, to remove the magenta)

changes.expected: The plaster and rug read as warm neutral grey or oat rather than salmon, and the red of the speakers separates from the room.

changes.problem: The speakers are darker than the floor and plinths, so they are not the hero.

evidence.measured: speaker lum_median 26.7 (left 27.0) against rug 117.8 and plinth top 100.6

change.from: 2 x 90 W, cone 18 deg, landing on the plinth tops
change.to: 2 x 110 W, cone 24 deg, re-aimed to the cabinet centre about 0.7 m above each plinth top, so the light passes through the acrylic onto the white batts

changes.expected: The cabinets glow from within, the woofers' surrounds are legible, and the plinth tops drop below the cabinets.

changes.problem: The rug is the brightest large surface and reads as a flat CG plane.

evidence.measured: lum_median 117.8, lum_range 143.7 from shadows only; no pile texture visible at 1:1

change.setting: the rug's material and the seats spot
change.from: smooth light salmon wool, seats spot 6.0 W cone 60 deg
change.to: a mid-dark undyed grey-brown wool (about #5A5249) with a displaced pile and bump and a visible bound edge showing concrete beyond it; seats spot 3.0 W

changes.expected: The floor falls into a mid-tone pool with real wool texture, below the speakers in brightness.

changes.problem: The left plaster wall is flat-lit and much brighter than the rest of the room.

evidence.measured: lum_median 113.1, p5 31.6: evenly lit, no falloff

change.setting: soft light: the room's fill; materials: the plaster

changes.expected: The plaster sits in shadow with a gentle gradient, framing the speakers rather than competing with them.

changes.problem: The back felt is washed hardest at the top, away from the subject, and its regular folds with specular lines read as metal fluting.

evidence.measured: falloff along y: 78.4 at the top falling to 18.4 at speaker height

change.setting: soft light: the back felt's wash; the felt's finish
change.from: 0.8 W/m2, aimed high; felt with a specular sheen
change.to: 0.5 W/m2 grazing up from the floor behind the plinths so it peaks at 0.8 to 1.6 m; felt roughness 1.0, specular 0, with a fibre/nap bump; fold depth and spacing varied by +/-30% (dressing only, the drape's position unchanged)

changes.expected: A soft pool of light on the felt behind and between the speakers, falling off upward into the dark ceiling; folds read as heavy cloth.

changes.problem: The chairs' oak is a saturated red-brown with the same grain on every chair, which brings a second colour into the frame and signals repeated copies.

evidence.measured: RGB median 124/62/39; identical figure on the visible chair backs

change.setting: the oak's stain; the chairs' texture mapping
change.to: natural oiled white oak (about #9C7E5E) with a random UV offset and rotation per chair and slight roughness variation; seat pads in charcoal wool rather than the rug's colour

changes.expected: The chairs read as natural oak, neutral beside the Ember speakers, each one different.

changes.problem: The 20 mm lens stretches the edges, and a cropped chair back fills the bottom right while the decks table and any practical sit out of frame.

evidence.measured: foreground slab occupying about 8% of the frame at median 43.6; left-edge chairs stretched

change.to: about 1.5 m further back toward the seat rows' centre aisle, 1.15 m high (seated), 28 mm, f/2.8 focused on the middle seat's sightline between the speakers; frame the decks table at one edge

changes.expected: A seated listener's view: both speakers and the decks in frame, true verticals, no stretched edge chairs, no foreground slab.

changes.problem: Nothing in the frame says this is a used listening room at EARF: no practical, no records, no life.

evidence.measured: no lamp or object brighter than the speakers apart from clipped panel edges; no props visible

change.setting: EARF's lamps: Core; small props; haze
change.from: Core 0.2 W, glow 0.005 (unlit or out of frame); no props; haze 0.0006
change.to: one Core on the decks table lit at 1.0 W, glow 0.02, in frame; a record out of its sleeve on the platter, the sleeve leaning on the table, a coat over one chair back, a programme card on a seat; haze 0.0015

changes.expected: A motivated warm practical and lived-in details; the spot beams get faint depth in the air.

out_of_scope.request: The resin horns read as near-black opaque lumps, and the metal stand-offs under the horns are visible
out_of_scope.why: This is the speaker's shape and parts, which the card fixes; only light (c2) can help.

out_of_scope.request: The red side panels read as flat glowing plastic, like signage
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's tint and construction are fixed; the light through the acrylic (c2) and the white balance (c1) are the only levers.
